Corollary
[Positive constant-curvature endpoints lie in the conjugate locus]

↗ cor:dc-ch5-3-3-first-conjugate ↗ def:dc-ch5-3-4 Under the hypotheses of the preceding corollary, if $p=\gamma (0)$ then $\gamma (\pi /\sqrt{K_0})\in C(p)$. Thus the intrinsic formalized consequence of the sphere calculation is that every such first endpoint belongs to the conjugate locus; identifying it with the antipode, and proving $C(p)=\{ -p\} $ for the round sphere, requires the additional global sphere geometry.
